draft.title: Bearings and elevation
card: True bearing
A true bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, written with three digits. East is 090°, south is 180° and a bearing of 45° is written 045°.
Elevation
An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal to the line of sight. An angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal.
Two steps

Draw a right-angled triangle. Use sin, cos or tan to find one side, then use that side in the next step. Example: a ship sails 10 km on a bearing of 090°, then 24 km on 180°. It is now √(10² + 24²) = √676 = 26 km from the start.
Back bearing
To find the bearing of A from B, when you know the bearing of B from A, add or subtract 180°. Keep the answer between 000° and 360°.
draft.remember: Bearings turn clockwise from north. Elevation and depression are measured from the horizontal.

a.q: A boat sails 15 km due east, then 20 km due south. How far is it from where it started?
a.why: The two legs meet at a right angle, so the distance is √(15² + 20²) = √625 = 25 km. Adding the legs to get 35 km is wrong, because the straight line back is the hypotenuse, not the sum of the two sides.
a.clue: East then south makes a right angle. Which side is the direct distance?

b.q: Town B is on a bearing of 060° from town A. What is the bearing of town A from town B?
b.why: The back bearing differs by 180°, so 060° + 180° = 240°. Taking 180° − 60° = 120° is tempting, but that treats the angle as measured from south and does not give the clockwise angle from north at B.
b.clue: The direction at B points the opposite way to the direction at A.

problems.detail: The 'Two steps' item says to use sin, cos or tan to find one side and then use it in the next step, but its example uses only Pythagoras in a single step. The example does not show the method it is meant to illustrate.
'Keep the answer between 000° and 360°' suggests 360° is a valid bearing. Bearings run from 000° up to but not including 360° (360° is written 000°).

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with single answers of 25 km and 240°. On the card, the two-step example uses Pythagoras rather than the sin/cos/tan method it describes, and the back-bearing range wrongly implies 360° is a valid bearing.

proposal.title: Bearings and elevation
card: True bearing
A true bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north, written with three digits. East is 090°, south is 180°, west is 270° and a bearing of 45° is written 045°.
Elevation

An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal to the line of sight. An angle of depression is measured down from the horizontal. The depression from A to B equals the elevation from B to A.
Two steps

Use sin, cos or tan in one right-angled triangle to find a shared side, then use it in the next. Example: 30 m from a tower the elevation is 40°, so height = 30 × tan 40° ≈ 25.2 m. Where the elevation is 25°, distance = 25.2 ÷ tan 25° ≈ 54.0 m.
Back bearing
To find the bearing of A from B, add 180° to the bearing of B from A, or subtract 180° if it is 180° or more. Bearings run from 000° up to 359°, and 360° is written 000°.
proposal.remember: Bearings turn clockwise from north. Elevation and depression both start at the horizontal.

a.q: A plane flies south-west. What is its true bearing?
a.why: South is 180° and west is 270°, so south-west lies halfway between them at 225°. The answer 135° comes from turning anticlockwise from north, but bearings always turn clockwise.
a.clue: Turn clockwise from north past south, but not as far as west.

b.q: From the top of a 60 m lighthouse, the angle of depression to a boat is 15°. Later it is 25°. How far has the boat moved toward the lighthouse?
b.why: The depression angle equals the elevation angle at the boat, so each distance is 60 ÷ tan of the angle: 60 ÷ tan 15° ≈ 223.9 m and 60 ÷ tan 25° ≈ 128.7 m. The boat moved 223.9 − 128.7 ≈ 95.3 m. Multiplying by tan instead of dividing gives 11.9 m, which treats the height as the side next to the angle.
b.clue: The height is opposite the angle at the boat in both triangles.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: south-west is 225°, and 60 ÷ tan 15° − 60 ÷ tan 25° ≈ 95.3 m. The card's worked example is also accurate.
